newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T drops on tobacco settlement doubts.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T drops on tobacco settlement doubts.

text.p: Shares in B.A.T Industries Plc dropped in early trade on Wednesday after a U.S. press report raised doubts about the proposed $368 billion U.S. tobacco settlement announced last month, dealers said.
The stock was down 7-1/2p at 541 by 0740 GMT in volume of 133,592 shares.

A report in the Washington Post said the White House would reject a key element of the proposed settlement because it would impose new restrictions on federal authorities to regulate nicotine in cigarettes.

Shares in B.A.T, whose U.S. unit Brown and Williamson was among the companies involved in the settlement, have risen sharply in recent months amid hopes that the deal would clarify the industry's liabilities under lawsuits for smoking-related diseases.
There have also been hopes that the settlement could pave the way for a long-awaited demerger of B.A.T's tobacco and insurance arms.

Yet the Washington Post quoted senior officials as saying the Clinton administration had decided to reject part of the deal after concluding that it surrendered too much of the Food and Drug Administration's ability to control the addictiveness of cigarettes.
Aides to President Clinton planned to rewrite the proposal and said the president was willing to walk away from the proposal if he could not amend it to his satisfaction, the newspaper said.
No-one at B.A.T was immediately available for comment.
